reason: The core holds, and it is not a repeat: rounds 5-15 contain no answer-parsing rule. It is also not a closed line or a mechanism. So it has no R8, dummy, byte-identity or runtime cost, and it needs no user OK as long as it only tightens how answers are read. The precedent is real. At 21:21Z (CONTEXT l.2466-2470), 'сделай нам также!' plus 'делай' was read as a retrain yes that lifted R8. R13-A3 (l.2722-2724) had to suspend that reading. There are 6 open questions against the 09:00Z, 12:00Z and ~12:15Z clocks, so a bare 'da' is genuinely ambiguous. There is no direct private score gain; the value is avoiding a wrong re-tick or an unauthorized push. Three parts are wrong or incomplete as written. (1) The finding reads 'yes to all' as Q1+Q2+Q3 yes. That LOOSENS R13-A3, which asks for three SEPARATE yes/no answers. Q1 is a head-only FT that would also override the user's own 25 Sep refusal (7) and R9 (see round16/scan_plancheck). Reading it that way repeats the over-reading this rule is meant to stop. (2) 'Yes to all' is ambiguous beyond class C (b) vs (c). With exp70b yes plus class C (b), the partner of V*_C could be #37 or exp70b (the INS gap in scan_plancheck). (3) Timing trap: if the session asks a clarifying question and the answer arrives after the first 43/44 terminal header, the class-C letter becomes post-hoc under R15-A1 (4).
fix:
Adopt, with these amendments, as one dated CONTEXT line (procedure; no rule change; no user OK):
(i) Q1, Q2 and Q3 (exp71 push, exp72 submit, exp72 final) each count only if the user names them. A blanket 'yes to all' / 'da na vse' does NOT authorise the exp71 push, per R13-A3 (separate yes/no) and the user's 25 Sep refusal (7). Ask about them explicitly in the checklist.
(ii) A blanket yes reads as: E10 v2 yes; exp70b yes; class C allowed, variant pending; cap unchanged. The checklist then asks two things: (b) vs (c), and whether (b)'s partner is exp70b or #37.
(iii) Log each letter verbatim, with `date -u`, AT ARRIVAL and before any clarifying reply. If the clarification has not come back by the first 56598763/56598765 terminal header, only 'class C allowed' counts as pre-registered. The variant is then labelled USER DECISION AFTER SCORE.
(iv) The one numbered checklist states each question's default and deadline (09:00Z, 12:00:00Z, ~12:15Z header, 28 Sep 18:30Z, 29 Sep 02:00Z), and sends no second nag.
(v) Before an irreversible step (the exp71 push, a re-tick instruction, a submit), echo the parsed answer back in one line. This is kept as in the finding.
realistic_gain: 0 direct score on public or private (no file changes). It is tail-risk governance: it lowers the chance of a mis-authorised push or re-tick. A wrong re-tick into an unverified class-C or retrain final is the only way this phase can lose a medal-relevant amount (the insertion-hedge cliff, P ~0.10-0.15 if the hedge is lost). Cost: ~5 min to write the CONTEXT line, and one extra chat round-trip when an answer is ambiguous.
